memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: After the flood Noah lived 350 years. Noah lived a total of 950 years, and then he died. - Gen 9:28-29 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter, and the story of Noah, closes with those familiar, sobering words that echoed all through the genealogy of chapter five: "and then he died." Noah lived an extraordinary 950 years, saw the old world destroyed and a new one begin, walked with God, and yet, like everyone before him, he came at last to the grave. Even the great survivor of the flood could not survive death.

There is a quiet lesson in this ending. However remarkable a life may be - however long, however faithful, however filled with mighty deeds - every earthly life comes to the same end. Noah's story reminds us of the shortness and fragility of life, and calls us to number our days wisely (Ps 90:12).

But notice that Noah's death is not the end of the story. God's purposes carried on through his sons and their descendants. The line of promise continued, moving steadily toward the coming of the Saviour. Individual lives end, but God's redemptive plan marches on, unbroken and unstoppable.

And for those who belong to God, death itself is not defeat but a doorway. Noah died, but he is listed among the faithful who look for "a better country - a heavenly one" (Heb 11:16). The One who came from Noah's line, Jesus Christ, has conquered death, so that all who trust Him can say that even in dying, they are not lost but gathered home. Noah's grave was not his end, and in Christ, it need not be ours.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you living each day in light of life's shortness and eternity's certainty?
- Have you placed your hope in Christ, who conquered the grave?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, teach me to number my days and live wisely in the time You give. Thank You that Your purposes never end, and that in Christ, death is not defeat but a doorway home. Hold my hope secure in You.
